Dear Colleagues

My name is Mahir Salihbašić, a soon-to-be graduate of applied mathematics at the University of Tuzla, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

My main interests lie in optimal control, especially differential games. However, ever since my first year studying mathematics, I’ve had an interest in formal theories and formalisation of mathematics. I worked with Rocq and on several occassions played around with Lean, but never actually worked on Mathlib itself.

Recently, I got involved in a research project as a student, with the project’s aim being exploring AI assisted formalisation of certain areas in control theory. My current assignment is to investigate traditional (i.e. no AI assistance) methodology of formalising proofs in Lean.

Which leads me to ask if there are any resources, papers or even blogs, which discuss various ways a formalisation project can be approached. I’ve seen some ideas, such as blueprints (from LTE), but I’m more interested in the practicalities and nuances of running a formalisation project that includes several people with varying levels of expertise: how is task allocation handled, abstraction level decided, project workflow planned etc.
Any resources or tips would be tremendously helpful.

I hope to be able to contribute to the community soon. Meanwhile, I send my greetings.

The reports about the Carleson and Equational Theories projects each had a section about this, and if you go on the leanprover community website, there are several papers that talk about the organizational aspects of mathlib.
